text:
micah: Quick flag from design review — the in-product docs panel uses 'model version' while the console dropdown label says 'variant' which is confusing for customers. Also the cross-link to the docs is tucked under a small 'Learn more' button rather than next to the setting. Screenshot: :camera: https://mock.redwood.test/screenshots/model-panel.png

tara: 100% agree. We swapped terms while shortening copy. My proposal: pick one term for all customer-facing surfaces. I lean toward 'Model variant' since it communicates runtime switching. Keep 'version' in the API reference only.

javi: From a design POV: +1 to 'Model variant'. Suggest we put a small inline info tooltip that says "previously called 'version'" for one release cycle. Also move the docs link inline next to the label (not the tiny footer button).

docs-bot: FYI I opened a draft PR to standardize the docs terminology: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pulls/42 — holding until product confirms. I can also add a 301 from /model-version -> /model-variant if we go forward.

andy: Implementation note: the in-product docs panel is a shared React component used across settings and flows. If we change the header text we must update the aria-label and ensure keyboard focus flows still work: currently focus lands on the panel body, but the close button isn't always visible to screen readers after open (focus trap issue).

olivia: @micah @tara good call. Let's standardize to 'Model variant' in all customer-facing UI; map 'version' in the API docs with a short note. @javi can you post the final copy for the panel? @docs-bot please hold the PR until we lock copy tomorrow.

javi: Copy suggestion for panel:
Header: "Model variant"
Body: "Select the model variant used for inference. Variants are runtime-compatible versions of models (was \"version\")."
Footer link text: "See model variant docs" (inline link to docs).
Accessible close button label: `Close model variant panel`

micah: Looks good. Small a11y nit — don't use generic link text like 'docs' or 'learn more' alone. Make the link descriptive and add a skip-to-content anchor for screen readers to jump back to the settings list after closing.

tara: I'll update the mock to move the cross-link inline next to the setting name and run keyboard/tab tests across panels. Will share updated frames in the design channel shortly. Thanks all :rocket:
